steps.title: Start the tonkotsu
steps.body: Blanch 1 kg pork bones, then simmer with water, ginger, and garlic for at least 4 hours. Skim foam, strain, and season with a splash of soy. Let it bubble away while you make the noodles.
steps.tip: Milky white color means you did it right — emulsified fat is the goal.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.body: Combine 300g bread flour, 150ml warm water, and ½ tsp salt. Stir until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
steps.tip: Dough should feel like a soft earlobe — firm but forgiving.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot tonkotsu broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming tonkotsu broth from step one. Serve straight — pure noodle confidence today.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming tonkotsu broth from step one. Lay warm chashu slices over the noodles. Spoon chili crisp on top as a finishing heat — this is separate from your dragon chili broth base. Halve a jammy soft-boiled egg and place yolk-side up. Crush roasted peanuts and sprinkle generously. Finish with sliced scallions on top. Scatter toasted sesame seeds for crunch — separate from your sesame dan dan broth base.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Start the tonkotsu
steps.body: Blanch 1 kg pork bones, then simmer with water, ginger, and garlic for at least 4 hours. Skim foam, strain, and season with a splash of soy. Let it bubble away while you make the noodles.
steps.tip: Milky white color means you did it right — emulsified fat is the goal.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your tonkotsu broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.
steps.tip: Par-cooking lets you prep ahead for ramen night.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming tonkotsu broth from step one. Serve straight — pure noodle confidence today.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Start the tonkotsu
steps.body: Blanch 1 kg pork bones, then simmer with water, ginger, and garlic for at least 4 hours. Skim foam, strain, and season with a splash of soy. Let it bubble away while you make the noodles.
steps.tip: Milky white color means you did it right — emulsified fat is the goal.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your tonkotsu broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.

steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your tonkotsu broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.
steps.tip: Par-cooking lets you prep ahead for ramen night.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming tonkotsu broth from step one. Lay warm chashu slices over the noodles. Halve a jammy soft-boiled egg and place yolk-side up. Scatter toasted sesame seeds for crunch — separate from your sesame dan dan broth base.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Start the tonkotsu
steps.body: Blanch 1 kg pork bones, then simmer with water, ginger, and garlic for at least 4 hours. Skim foam, strain, and season with a splash of soy. Let it bubble away while you make the noodles.
steps.tip: Milky white color means you did it right — emulsified fat is the goal.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your tonkotsu broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.
steps.tip: Par-cooking lets you prep ahead for ramen night.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming tonkotsu broth from step one. Lay warm chashu slices over the noodles. Spoon chili crisp on top as a finishing heat — this is separate from your dragon chili broth base. Crush roasted peanuts and sprinkle generously. Finish with sliced scallions on top.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Start the tonkotsu
steps.body: Blanch 1 kg pork bones, then simmer with water, ginger, and garlic for at least 4 hours. Skim foam, strain, and season with a splash of soy. Let it bubble away while you make the noodles.
steps.tip: Milky white color means you did it right — emulsified fat is the goal.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Build the chili broth base
steps.body: Heat half a cup of neutral oil until shimmering. Pour over chili flakes, minced garlic, and Sichuan peppercorn. Stir in soy and a pinch of sugar. This is your dragon chili broth — not the chili crisp topping later.
steps.tip: Pour the hot oil from high — the sizzle is the whole point.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.body: Combine 300g bread flour, 150ml warm water, and ½ tsp salt. Stir until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
steps.tip: Dough should feel like a soft earlobe — firm but forgiving.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot dragon chili broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming dragon chili broth from step one. Serve straight — pure noodle confidence today.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot dragon chili broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming dragon chili broth from step one. Finish with sliced scallions on top.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Build the chili broth base
steps.body: Heat half a cup of neutral oil until shimmering. Pour over chili flakes, minced garlic, and Sichuan peppercorn. Stir in soy and a pinch of sugar. This is your dragon chili broth — not the chili crisp topping later.
steps.tip: Pour the hot oil from high — the sizzle is the whole point.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.body: Combine 300g bread flour, 150ml warm water, and ½ tsp salt. Stir until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
steps.tip: Dough should feel like a soft earlobe — firm but forgiving.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot dragon chili broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot dragon chili broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming dragon chili broth from step one. Lay warm chashu slices over the noodles. Spoon chili crisp on top as a finishing heat — this is separate from your dragon chili broth base. Crush roasted peanuts and sprinkle generously. Finish with sliced scallions on top.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Build the chili broth base
steps.body: Heat half a cup of neutral oil until shimmering. Pour over chili flakes, minced garlic, and Sichuan peppercorn. Stir in soy and a pinch of sugar. This is your dragon chili broth — not the chili crisp topping later.
steps.tip: Pour the hot oil from high — the sizzle is the whole point.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.body: Combine 300g bread flour, 150ml warm water, and ½ tsp salt. Stir until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
steps.tip: Dough should feel like a soft earlobe — firm but forgiving.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish

steps.title: Build the chili broth base

steps.title: Make alkaline dough

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets

steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Build the chili broth base
steps.body: Heat half a cup of neutral oil until shimmering. Pour over chili flakes, minced garlic, and Sichuan peppercorn. Stir in soy and a pinch of sugar. This is your dragon chili broth — not the chili crisp topping later.
steps.tip: Pour the hot oil from high — the sizzle is the whole point.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your dragon chili broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.
steps.tip: Par-cooking lets you prep ahead for ramen night.

steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your dragon chili broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming dragon chili broth from step one. Lay warm chashu slices over the noodles. Halve a jammy soft-boiled egg and place yolk-side up. Crush roasted peanuts and sprinkle generously.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Build the chili broth base
steps.body: Heat half a cup of neutral oil until shimmering. Pour over chili flakes, minced garlic, and Sichuan peppercorn. Stir in soy and a pinch of sugar. This is your dragon chili broth — not the chili crisp topping later.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.

steps.title: Whisk the sesame broth base
steps.body: Combine 3 tbsp sesame paste, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, and half a cup of warm stock until silky smooth. This is your sesame dan dan broth — separate from any sesame seed topping.
steps.tip: Thin with hot stock, not water — it keeps the nutty flavor.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.body: Combine 300g bread flour, 150ml warm water, and ½ tsp salt. Stir until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
steps.tip: Dough should feel like a soft earlobe — firm but forgiving.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot sesame dan dan broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming sesame dan dan broth from step one. Serve straight — pure noodle confidence today.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Boil & slurp
steps.body: Boil in salted rolling water 2–3 minutes until they float and taste chewy. Rinse briefly if serving cold, or ladle straight into the hot sesame dan dan broth you started in step one.
steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming sesame dan dan broth from step one. Halve a jammy soft-boiled egg and place yolk-side up.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Whisk the sesame broth base
steps.body: Combine 3 tbsp sesame paste, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, and half a cup of warm stock until silky smooth. This is your sesame dan dan broth — separate from any sesame seed topping.
steps.tip: Thin with hot stock, not water — it keeps the nutty flavor.

steps.tip: Fresh noodles cook fast — taste at 90 seconds.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your hand-pulled thick noodles into the steaming sesame dan dan broth from step one. Lay warm chashu slices over the noodles. Crush roasted peanuts and sprinkle generously.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Whisk the sesame broth base
steps.body: Combine 3 tbsp sesame paste, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, and half a cup of warm stock until silky smooth. This is your sesame dan dan broth — separate from any sesame seed topping.
steps.tip: Thin with hot stock, not water — it keeps the nutty flavor.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.body: Combine 300g bread flour, 150ml warm water, and ½ tsp salt. Stir until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
steps.tip: Dough should feel like a soft earlobe — firm but forgiving.

steps.title: Rest & knead again
steps.body: Wrap in plastic and rest 30 minutes. Knead 2 more minutes — the gluten relaxes and the pull gets easier.
steps.tip: Skip the rest and the noodles snap instead of stretch.

steps.title: Oil & coil
steps.body: Brush the dough with neutral oil. Roll into a long snake and coil it into a tight spiral on an oiled tray.
steps.tip: Oil is your insurance policy against sticking.

steps.title: Pull the strands
steps.body: Hold both ends, bounce gently, fold in half, and repeat. Each fold doubles the strands — aim for pencil-thin noodles.
steps.tip: Pull over the pot so they drop straight into boiling water.

steps.title: Make alkaline dough
steps.body: Mix 300g high-protein flour with 120ml water plus 1 tsp baked baking soda dissolved in warm water (kansui substitute). Knead until tight.
steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your sesame dan dan broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.
steps.tip: Par-cooking lets you prep ahead for ramen night.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming sesame dan dan broth from step one. Serve straight — pure noodle confidence today.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.tip: Alkaline water gives ramen its signature yellow color and chew.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.
steps.tip: Cold rest makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.
steps.tip: Cornstarch, not flour — it keeps strands separate.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.
steps.tip: Uneven cuts cook unevenly — slow down on the last fold.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your sesame dan dan broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.
steps.tip: Par-cooking lets you prep ahead for ramen night.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming sesame dan dan broth from step one. Spoon chili crisp on top as a finishing heat — this is separate from your dragon chili broth base. Halve a jammy soft-boiled egg and place yolk-side up. Scatter toasted sesame seeds for crunch — separate from your sesame dan dan broth base.
steps.tip: Eat while the noodles still have bounce — timing is everything.

steps.title: Whisk the sesame broth base
steps.body: Combine 3 tbsp sesame paste, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, and half a cup of warm stock until silky smooth. This is your sesame dan dan broth — separate from any sesame seed topping.
steps.tip: Thin with hot stock, not water — it keeps the nutty flavor.

steps.body: Wrap tightly and rest 1 hour at room temperature — or overnight in the fridge for extra chew.

steps.title: Roll thin sheets
steps.body: Divide dough, flatten with a rolling pin or pasta machine to about 1.5mm thick. Dust lightly with cornstarch between folds.

steps.title: Cut the noodles
steps.body: Fold the sheet accordion-style and slice into 2mm strips with a sharp knife. Shake loose and dust again.

steps.title: Par-boil & finish
steps.body: Boil 60–90 seconds, drain, and rinse once. Reheat in your sesame dan dan broth for 30 seconds before serving — never overcook twice.

steps.title: Top your bowl
steps.body: Ladle your silk-thin noodles into the steaming sesame dan dan broth from step one. Spoon chili crisp on top as a finishing heat — this is separate from your dragon chili broth base.
